question: Can the MMSU catalog record for the Oaig-Upay-Abulao River undergraduate thesis support species assertions, and is the thesis available for authorized review?

method.summary: Screened the Mariano Marcos State University Library catalog record and its indexed abstract. A direct page open timed out; the catalog search result exposes the bibliographic record, abstract and item-status fields. The record says the physical thesis is available in the MMSU Main Library, Theses and Dissertation Section, marked Room Use Only. No digital thesis, station table, species checklist, image, water-quality values or license text was retrieved.
method.accessFinding: Cataloged as a 66-leaf undergraduate BS Environmental Science thesis, with one library holding at MMSU Main Library marked Available / Room Use Only. The record exposes no downloadable full-text file. This means the thesis is an access-limited lead; do not infer permission to download, scan, reproduce or redistribute its contents.
method.abstractEvidenceLimit: The indexed catalog abstract summarizes the thesis but is not the thesis methods/results chapter or raw dataset. The listed 14-species total and three named fish are retained as catalog-abstract reports only. Station-specific identities and counts, coordinates, vouchers, full taxon list, and independently checked identifications are unavailable.

study.citation: Mapalo, A. J. E., & Rigua, J. R. (2021). Macrofaunal Diversity Assessment of Oaig-Upay-Abulao River in Paoay, Ilocos Norte [Undergraduate thesis, Mariano Marcos State University].
study.studyDesignAsReported: The abstract describes experimental, correlational and descriptive designs; three designated river sampling stations; water-quality assessment; and a questionnaire on human activities within and along the river.

catalogReportedFindings.scope: Macrofauna; the catalog abstract identifies fish among the reported organisms but does not provide the complete taxon list or station-by-taxon matrix.
catalogReportedFindings.abundanceWording: The catalog abstract calls Platax orbicularis the most abundant, followed by Oreochromis niloticus and Leiognathus fasciatus; no underlying counts or station allocation are provided in the catalog record.
catalogReportedFindings.habitatWording: The abstract says its TDS, salinity and electrical-conductivity levels were above normal freshwater levels and describes the result as more indicative of estuarine waters. No numeric station measurements or independent salinity classification are available in the catalog record.

study.spatialLimit: The title and catalog abstract place the study at Oaig-Upay-Abulao River in Paoay, Ilocos Norte and report three designated sampling stations. They provide no station names, coordinates, reach descriptions, station-by-taxon table or specimen-to-station crosswalk. Do not assign the river-wide abstract taxa to the barangay bearing the same name, individual stations, a river geometry or legal boundary without the thesis and independent locality evidence.
study.rightsFinding: No copyright license, open license or permission for thesis data, tables, figures or photos was verified. The MMSU catalog marks the physical holding Room Use Only and exposes no digital copy; this is an access condition, not a reuse license.

interpretation: This is a useful inland-water research lead for Region I, but only the library catalog and its indexed abstract were screened. The undergraduate thesis itself was not retrieved or reviewed.

The catalog abstract reports 14 macrofauna taxa and names three fish labels, but no complete taxa list, numeric fish abundance, sampling gear details, voucher/accession IDs or station-level results are available from the catalog record.

The abstract's estuarine-water interpretation is a source-reported inference. Without the thesis values, station context and independent salinity evidence, do not classify every reach as freshwater, brackish or estuarine or make water-safety claims.
A 2021 study is historical context, not evidence of present occurrence, abundance, catchability, diet, bait suitability, access, legality or current water safety.

No species assertions, occurrence rows, waterbody geometry, public app data, images or derived water-quality advice are added. The thesis remains research-only until it can be reviewed under its library access conditions and its reuse terms are clarified.

decision.reason: The public MMSU catalog exposes an abstract for a relevant 2021 river thesis, but its physical copy is marked Room Use Only and no full text, station-level evidence, vouchers or reuse license was retrieved. Treat the abstract as a research lead only.

nextAction: Continue searching for a publicly readable, independently reusable freshwater or estuarine fish survey for Ilocos Norte. If this thesis is later consulted in person under the MMSU library's room-use conditions, separately verify the complete taxa table, sampling stations, voucher information and reuse terms before recording detailed evidence.
